name: Branislav Brzak
bio: Branislav Brzak is an AI security researcher at Stealthium and a member of the Stealthium Core Team. His focus is low-level GPU security research, together with Linux kernel, virtualization, and performance engineering. He is the author of the Stealthium research post "Return of a Nosy Neighbor: More Detail, More Noise" (September 2026), which extends the USENIX Security '26 "Behind Bars" work on NVIDIA MIG. It shows that a GPU co-tenant can fingerprint a victim LLM's architecture and depth with about 97% accuracy and its decode speed with about 99.3% accuracy from timing alone, both within a MIG-partitioned H100 and across an NVSwitch/NVLink fabric. His AI Engineer NYC 2026 lunch talk presented this research. Based in Serbia.

sessions.title: Extra lunch talk: what a GPU co-tenant can learn about your LLM from timing alone (MIG and NVLink side channels)
